To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
inhibitors of prostaglndin synthesis inhibit production of infectious HCMV in a productively infected cell line and reactivation of the latently infected HCMV in an in vitro model system.
indomethacin and related compounds, inhibitors of prostglandin synthesis, inhibit the growth of human cytromealovirus and reacivation of the latent virus in a human thyroid cell line (TP-1).
indomethacin and other prostaglandin inhibitors inhibit HCMV growth in vitro by inhibiting early viral gene transcription.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a possible role of prostaglandins in the regulation of the growth of human cytotoxic viruses.
the possible role of prostaglandins in the control of virus replication.
the effect of prostaglandins on HCMV replication and reactivation of latently infected cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prostaglandin inhibitors inhibit the early stages of HCMV infection and prevent reactivation of the latently infected virus in the TPC-1 cell line.
indomethacin and/or tetracaine inhibit the production of infectious HCMV and the reactivation of latent HCMV in TPC- 1 cell cultures by inhibiting the synthesis of prostaglandins.
the inhibitors of prostaglanding synthesis inhibit the growth of HCMV in TPC- 1 cells and reactivation of the latently infected virus in TPC- I cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
indomethacin and/or tetracaine may be useful for the prevention of HCMV infections in humans.
the prostaglandins may be involved in the regulation of the early stages of virus growth and in the reactivation of latent HCMV.
the prostaglandins are important in the regulation of both productive and latent HCMV infections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
indomethacin and other inhibitors of prostaglanin synthesis may be useful for the treatment of HCMV infections.
indomethacin and other inhibitors of prostagladin synthesis can be used to inhibit the growth of HCMV and to inhibit reactivation of latent HCMV.
